_readme: Product marketing framework, schema v2 (19 Nov 2026), for the Eclipse Smart-Heat® Electric collection: Eclipse Electric on its six pole and wall mounts and Eclipse Freestanding (the "Eclipse Portable" of manuals and older pages). Matrix 1: what matters to each buyer across twelve benefit fields (w: 3 matters most, 2 matters, 1 nice to have) and the claim that resonates. Matrix 2: Platinum Smart-Heat® Electric (left) against Eclipse (right), to place the round, design-led heater against the linear one. Matrix 3: Eurofase Vellura, Heatsail DOME and Kettler Kalos (factual, sourced, needs_approval Specification and compliance). Bromic facts from data/product-facts.json, the 2026 cut sheets and the 2025 US manuals; claims add no new facts. Prices are directional, never in ads.
name: Eclipse Smart-Heat® Electric

launch.summary: Eclipse is Bromic’s design-led electric heater: the one collection that pairs radiant heat with a dimmable LED ring, hung from six poles or standing on its own arch. It is for spaces where the heater is seen and the light matters: dining terraces, hotel and restaurant canopies, pavilions and lounges with no roof.

m2_label.intro: When the round, design-led heater beats the linear one, and when it does not.

m2.s2: Dimmable warm white LED ring, 3000K, 497 lm on Eclipse Electric (216.6 lm listed for Freestanding [[VERIFY: freestanding lumens; both manuals give 20 W at 24 V DC — Product team]]).
m2.so_what: Where the ceiling also needs light, Eclipse does two jobs in one fixture.

m2.s1: Recessed, ceiling or wall; 8 in stainless pole included; recess kits and longer poles sold separately.
m2.s2: Six pole and wall options (24 in twin pole included) and a freestanding version; Eclipse cannot be recessed.
m2.so_what: Flush in the ceiling, choose Platinum. Hanging, arching or standing as a feature, choose Eclipse.

m2.s1: Slim linear body in Black or White; minimal and architectural.
m2.s2: Round 27.6 in disc in matte black with a radial ceramic screen and LED halo.
m2.so_what: Platinum disappears into the architecture; Eclipse is the statement piece.

m2.s1: 2,300, 3,400 and 4,500 W; up to 65, 108 and 143 ft²; dimmable in 1% steps with the Affinity Dimmer.
m2.s2: One output, 2,900 W, up to 121 ft²; three heat steps (33, 66, 100%).
m2.so_what: For the most heat per fixture or fine dimming, Platinum 4,500 W; for even warmth table by table with light, Eclipse.

m2.s1: Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off or Dimmer, sold separately; up to 6 kW a channel; manual wall switch.
m2.s2: Affinity Smart-Heat® Eclipse Controller, sold separately: one heater a channel, heat and light from the app; Eclipse Freestanding includes its Eclipse Dimmer Controller and remote.
m2.so_what: Both run on the Bromic app; Eclipse adds light scenes, and needs one channel for each heater.

m2.s1: Electric infrared, no flame or fumes; minimum 72 in on a wall, 96 in on a ceiling; Intertek ETL/cETL.
m2.s2: Electric infrared, no flame or fumes; minimum 96 in on a wall or ceiling, 79 in for Freestanding; SGS listed for the US and Canada.
m2.so_what: Same peace of mind; Platinum can sit lower on a wall.

m2.s1: 304 stainless chassis; Platinum Marine in 316 stainless, IPX5, Lloyd’s Register approved. [[VERIFY: Platinum Classic IP rating — Product team]]
m2.s2: Double-coated steel, IP54 [[VERIFY: material, the site FAQ says 304 stainless — Product team]]; manual advises mounting under cover.
m2.so_what: By the sea or exposed to weather, Platinum (Marine). Under a roof, canopy or pergola, either.

m2.s1: Cut sheets, manuals, recess guidance and the complimentary design service.
m2.s2: Cut sheets, manuals, pole clearance drawings and the complimentary design service.
m2.so_what: Ask the design team to mix both: Platinum for coverage, Eclipse where light and form matter.

m2.s2: Eclipse Freestanding: arched arm, weighted base on two wheels, 15 ft cable and plug, 220 to 240 V.
m2.so_what: Where there is no ceiling or wall, Eclipse is the electric answer in this pair.

m2.s1: Up to 6 kW a channel on Affinity On/Off or Dimmer: often two heaters a channel.
m2.s2: One heater a channel; up to five on the 5-channel Eclipse controller.
m2.so_what: Large heated areas on few channels, Platinum; individually controlled tables with light, Eclipse.

m2.s1: 3 years (Platinum Marine: 5 years on land, 3 on vessels).
17 to 33 lb; 208 V and 220 to 240 V; recessing needs a recess kit and the right cavity.
m2.s2: 30 lb head on a pole kit included in the box; 208 V and 240 V pendant heads; no recess work.
m2.so_what: Eclipse goes up on a pole with no cavity to prepare; Platinum rewards the early drawing with a flush finish.

m3.intro: Eclipse against the round heat-and-light fixtures a buyer compares it with: a US decorative lighting brand, a Belgian design brand sold through US furniture retailers, and the UK mass market. Factual and sourced; each maker measures coverage its own way.

competitors.name: Eurofase Vellura (pendant EFH0139 and freestanding EFH0138)
competitors.owner: Eurofase Inc. (named in the Vellura manual)
competitors.why_closest: The US product that sells the same idea: heat and a 3000K LED light in one round decorative fixture, as a pendant and a freestanding lamp, through lighting showrooms and online. Lower output and price tier, plug-in 120 V.

competitors.name: Heatsail DOME (pendant, wall and bow brackets, floor lamp)
competitors.owner: Heatsail NV, Belgium; Heatsail USA Inc., Texas
competitors.why_closest: The closest design-tier match: a round far-infrared heater with integrated dimmable light, as a pendant, wall or bow bracket and an arched freestanding floor lamp, sold in the US through premium furniture retailers at a price near Eclipse.

competitors.name: Kettler Kalos pendant heaters (Universal, Plush)
competitors.why_closest: The UK and Irish mass-market version of heat and light from one round pendant: halogen heat, an LED light and a remote, at a fraction of the price. The benchmark homeowners in the UK find first.

rows.bromic: Dimmable warm white LED ring, 3000K, 497 lm (Eclipse Electric cut sheet), 20 W at 24 V DC on its own circuit; light dims in presets and 1% steps from the remote. [[VERIFY: light-only operation with heat off, and Freestanding lumens (216.6 lm listed) — Product team]]

vs.eurofase: Integrated LED, "3000K; 700 lumens", on/off and brightness from the remote; heat "Adjustable, up to 1500W" (EFH0139 manual).
vs.heatsail: "Light max. 120 Watt", dimmable with the remote and usable "with or without the heating" (DOME brochure); lumens not published.
vs.kalos: Universal pendant "Fitted with LED Light"; Plush LED switched separately by remote (retailer); lumens not published.

battlecard.objection: I can get a heater with a light for a few hundred dollars.
battlecard.answer: Plug-in heat-and-light pendants run at up to 1,500–2,000 W on a remote. Eclipse delivers 2,900 W in three settings, hard-wired and IP54, with app control through Affinity Smart-Heat® Controls.
True: Eclipse is matte black. It offers six pole options and a freestanding arch, 208 V and 240 V heads listed for the US and Canada, and app control with zones and schedules.
Where the ceiling should stay clean, we recommend Platinum Smart-Heat® Electric. Where you also need light, or the heater is part of the look, Eclipse does both.

battlecard.objection: Can I plug the freestanding one into my patio outlet?
battlecard.answer: Eclipse Freestanding needs a 220–240 V outdoor outlet rated IP54 or better; your electrician can add one. It rolls on two wheels when you rearrange.
Eclipse is IP54 and wind resistant, and the freestanding base is rated for winds up to 20 mph. For the longest life, we recommend mounting it under cover.

battlecard.objection: One controller channel per heater sounds expensive.
battlecard.answer: It means each table can be dimmed and scheduled on its own, heat and light. The 5-channel controller runs five heaters and includes the expansion board.
